chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from a number of his companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqub ibn Salim, who raised it to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Let the first thing eaten by the postpartum woman be fresh ripe dates (rutab), for Allah the Exalted said to Maryam: And shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree, it will drop on you fresh ripe dates.'

It was said, 'O Rasool-Allah! Suppose it is not the season for the fresh dates?' He said: 'Seven dates from the dates of Al-Medina. So if they are not available, then seven dates from the dates of your cities.'

For Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'By My Might, and My Majesty, and My Greatness, and the Elevation of My Status! A woman who eats fresh dates on the day she gives birth, if it is a boy, he will be forbearing (patient), and if it is a girl, she will be forbearing.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended food for a woman after childbirth according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a Sunnah for postpartum recovery by linking the consumption of fresh dates to the divine revelation given to Maryam (AS) in Surah Maryam, thereby grounding the practice in Quranic precedent. It further specifies a spiritual benefit, asserting that eating these dates on the day of childbirth fosters patience (hilm) in the newborn, a virtue highly prized in Shia ethical teachings. The hierarchy of date types—fresh, then Medina, then local—reflects the scholarly emphasis on both physical nourishment and the symbolic purity associated with the Prophet's homeland.
